**Analysis:**

The test image (Bugwood 5530077, photographer Bruce Watt) shows:
- Microscopic view at 100 μm scale
- Many small, round, translucent spherical spores (~15-25 μm each)
- Densely clustered in a grape-like arrangement
- On branching, transparent hyphae/conidiophores
- Dark background typical of brightfield microscopy

This is the textbook microscopic appearance of **Botrytis cinerea** (Gray Mold). The name "Botrytis" literally derives from Greek "botrys" (bunch of grapes), directly describing this grape-like cluster of conidia on branching conidiophores. No other class in the candidate list produces this distinctive microscopic morphology:
- Rhizopus: large dark solid sporangia (completely different, confirmed visually)
- Powdery Mildew: chains of barrel-shaped conidia, not grape clusters
- Late Blight/Phytophthora: lemon-shaped sporangia
- All other reference images showed macroscopic symptoms, none resembling this microscopic pattern
